One matching QC row; author replication test passes; both reported FRiP values at least 1%; overlapping author union regions labelled NOT-HOT; no identified target-label conflict.
The 1% cutoff is an explicit Atlas review filter, not a universal quality threshold or the authors’ replication-pass definition.
Uses the authors’ union-region annotation; high-occupancy, conflicting and unassessed classifications are excluded.
Peak observations across assay contexts, not unique sites or independent donors.
Author GRanges starts were converted from 1-based to 0-based by subtracting one; exclusive ends equal the converted start plus GRanges width.
The experiments share four postmortem donors across regions. Repeated contexts do not establish population replication.
Assayed targets include chromatin-associated proteins and cofactors as well as transcription factors. ChIP-seq measures regional occupancy; it does not locate a contact nucleotide.
Overlaps with existing ENCODE and PsychSCREEN brain candidate regulatory regions are spatial context, not independent validation of OXTR regulation.

13 author-packaged peak datasets and 226 additional public portal peak files inspected. The browser retains the conservative subset; all 390 locus observations, including histone marks, remain in the review download.
No nominal allele-specific result in the separately reviewed BrainTF table passed BH-adjusted P < 0.05 at this locus; none is presented as confirmed allele-specific binding.

OCE1, OCE5 and OCE7 enhanced reporter activity in mouse hypothalamic cells. The tested DNA was human. OCE7 also drove reporter activity in mouse olfactory bulb at P28 and P56; adult hypothalamic activity was not detected.
OCE2, OCE6 and OCE7 reported regions intersect the current window. OCE2 and OCE6 were negative in the reporter assay. The window is unchanged.
Reporter activity does not establish a named transcription-factor binding site or causal regulation of native human OXTR.
The reported OCE7 candidate interval and the Table 1 luciferase-primer span differ. Reported intervals and primer matches are retained separately, without a precise binding-site overlay.
